checks: Normalized exponentials represent uniform barycentric volume. The weighted density at zero is P_i=f db_i by the two accepted predecessors. There are at least three nonzero phases, so the coordinate eliminated in the conditional-law formula can be taken distinct from the coordinate whose mean is computed. A zero phase is independent and has conditional mean one. Deleting it changes neither the probability nor the ratios P_i/f of the nonzero phases.

For p>q, integrated the two-phase survival and density against the negative-phase sum. Direct differentiation of F=X+q(X−Y)/(p−q) gives P_q/f=1/h−ρS/(1−ρ), since q∂_qY=YS. Differentiation in −r_j gives (s_j−ρt_j)/(1−ρ), and t_j/s_j=1−ha_j.

For the scalar estimate, E² contains coefficient 2^k−2 on a squarefree degree-k term, greater than k−1 for k≥2, and includes positive squared singletons. With law e_k/E on k−1, the decreasing probability ratios make T_s/p_s nonincreasing. Multiplying tail ratios gives T_(a+b)≤T_a T_b. The ordered-positive-composition count recovers the binomial moment, bounded by the corresponding power of the mean. Finite support gives strict geometric domination when the mean and parameter are positive.

Checked AΣx_j=E+C, z=(E+C)/(AE), 1−z=(E²−C)/(AE) and the product identity from 1+τx_j=(1+(A/E)u_j)/(1+u_j). These imply the claimed scalar inequality with strictness for at least two entries. Supplementary exact-rational checks covered all 1,364 tuples over four test values of x in lengths one through five.
The map x_j=ha_j gives z=LS, and b_q≤1/d is exactly LS≥1−h. With one negative phase the scalar bound is equality but z=1−ha_1>1−h, which supplies strictness in the final comparison.

At p=q=1, the Gamma(2,1) density and survival give f=LZ and F=L(1+Z). Differentiation and Euler homogeneity give the stated negative and positive means. Multiplying the remaining means gives LZ(1+s)Π(1+v_j)/2. The assumed centroid condition is Z(1+s)≤2. The probability-vector result is strict with two or more negatives, and with one negative Z<1 gives strictness in the final comparison.

The source formulas and scopes agree with f942bc6e02fdf1dd §§2–3, 4ac6f62135b1565c §§1 and 3, and 5f357f58008cdf1e §§1–3. The optional unequal-height other-vertex corollary is a separate source claim.

The proper cut has heights of both signs, so its coarea conditional law has Gamma(d,1) radius independent of the uniform angular section. Conditional coordinate means equal d times the barycentric section centroid.

The vector v_j=t_j/Z is nonnegative and sums to one, so the product bound and its equality criterion apply. The elementary-symmetric convolution identity in its proof also applies to the positive u_j of the unequal-height scalar step.
